QUESTION OF THE WEEK - What's the percentage chance of another rate cut this cycle? A question which would have drawn scoffing laughter and a line of zeros a few weeks ago has become topical since March unemployment data showed the second successive monthly fall in employment.
A setback in the recovery of housing finance commitments and a run of subdued partial price indicators added to the feeling another easing was not unthinkable.

Analysts reckon if the award on the living wage claim next week equates to less than A$15 a week and the Q1 underlying inflation data do show the annual growth rate at the bottom of the Reserve Bank's 2-3 percent range, then the scope could be there for a cut in official rates, should the RBA judge the economic recovery is not meeting its upbeat expectations. ----------------------------------------------------------------

CONSUMER PRICES - Analysts expect the key annual underlying rate of inflation to slow for the fourth successive quarter to reach 2.0 percent in the March quarter. That would be well down on the 3.3 percent cycle peak hit in Q1 1996, the lowest growth since Q1 of 1995 and the very bottom of the Reserve Bank's 2-3 percent target range.

Bankers Trust pointed to a number of factors depressing prices, including excessive stock levels, strong competition in the retail sector in the face of modest consumer demand, a strong exchange rate, subdued inflation excpectations and modest growth in nominal unit labour costs.

Headline CPI should slow even faster as the effect of falling mortage and credit card rates feed through -- these are stripped out of the underlying calculation along with a host of prices deemed not directly determined by demand. This should largely offset expected rises in the food, health and personal care, and recreation and education groups in the CPI.

If annual CPI fall to 1.2 percent as expected it would be the lowest rate since the March quarter of 1993 when it was also 1.2 percent. Furthermore, were the CPI to fall in the quarter, as a few believe, it would be the first such drop since the June quarter of 1992.
